implementation_notes: C has no messaging stdlib, and librabbitmq is a protocol client, not an endpoint framework: the endpoint is a hand-written translation unit that owns the amqp_connection_state_t and its socket, opens a channel, declares/binds the queue, calls amqp_basic_consume() and drives the amqp_consume_message() loop, handing payload bytes to application functions. The classic full structure stays justified because nothing above the protocol layer exists; librabbitmq's README adds the constraint that a connection, socket or channel must not be shared between threads, so an endpoint per thread (or an explicit locking design) is required.
pitfalls: librabbitmq connections, sockets and channels are not thread-safe and cannot be shared between threads; use one connection per thread or an external locking scheme.
Every amqp_consume_message() result owns buffers that must be released with amqp_destroy_envelope() (plus amqp_maybe_release_buffers() between iterations) or the consumer leaks per delivery.
A NULL timeout on amqp_consume_message() blocks forever; a stalled broker silently parks the endpoint unless you bound the wait and handle the failure.
